verdict.rationale: First-party docs say that signing in to your Google Account on a new device automatically syncs your codes there, which is a one-step migration. For users without an account, a documented QR export on the old phone and scan on the new phone transfers codes, and community users confirm the export bundles all codes into one QR code. Complaints that codes were missing from OS phone backups concern the host platform's backup, not the product's own transfer flow, so they don't contradict it. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of the cloud-sync migration end to end, and a seamless path for users who lack the old device and don't use a Google Account.

support.subject: As an everyday user, moving to a new phone transfers all my tokens in one guided step

citations.quote: When you sign in to your Google Account within Google Authenticator on a new device, your codes are automatically synced to this device.
On your old device, create a QR code... On your new device, tap Scan QR code
Google Authenticator has a feature to allow export of all saved codes into one QR code for re-import into Google Authenticator running on another device.
